evidence.source: Xiaoxuetang (Academia Sinica), 字形演變資料庫
evidence.text: The database describes coverage of oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, small-seal and regular-script forms, and says its evolution view presents forms from Shang oracle-bone through Western Zhou bronze, Warring States and small seal to clerical script. It identifies the database as developed by National Taiwan University and Academia Sinica institutes and maintained by Academia Sinica's Center for Digital Cultures.

evidence.source: 汉典, quoting 《说文解字》 and Duan Yucai's commentary
evidence.text: The entry quotes 尦也。从子無臂。象形 and its account of a form derived from 子 without arms. Duan Yucai interprets 尦 as legs crossing in movement and explains 了戾 as twisted or knotted things that do not extend straight; he also reports borrowing for 憭悟. These are historical interpretations, not direct proof of the depicted referent or an inscriptional development sequence.
evidence.title: 了 liǎo、le - 汉典

evidence.text: Search result identifies its base text as the 四部丛刊初编 edition and displays the Shuowen wording 从子无臂. Opening the page returned 403, so only the search result was inspected.
evidence.title: 說文解字 : 卷十五 : 了部

search_audit.query: 了 字形演变 甲骨文 金文 小篆 字源 site:dict.variants.moe.edu.tw OR site:xiaoxuetang. sinica.edu.tw; 小學堂 了 字形 演變 4E86 Academia Sinica; Wikimedia Commons 了 Chinese character seal script image; 了 Shuowen 尦也 从子无臂 段玉裁 说文 原文
search_audit.outcome: Inspected official Xiaoxuetang overview, rights notice and scope documentation; opened Han Dian's character entry and Commons' 了 seal-SVG file page. CText search result exposed the received Shuowen wording, but its page returned 403. Xiaoxuetang's query UI did not yield a character-specific result page/image in this browser session.

search_audit.query: site:xiaoxue.iis.sinica.edu.tw/yanbian 了 1-4427 字形; site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File 了 seal script Chinese character
search_audit.outcome: Found and opened the Commons file page for a modern Shuowen seal-style SVG with explicit public-domain status. Xiaoxuetang query pages exposed database interface but did not return the character-specific glyph result through this tool; verified its official CC0 notice.

gaps: This pass did not establish an independently dated earliest attestation for 了 or confirm a paleographic sequence from oracle-bone or bronze inscriptions. Xiaoxuetang's database scope is documented, but the character-specific query result and its image URLs were not retrieved here.

No ancient artifact photograph was inspected. The proposed Commons candidate is explicitly a modern vector redraw of a Shuowen seal-style form; it illustrates the received dictionary form, not an excavated object or the competing crossed-legs/arm-less-child analyses independently.

No Xiaoxuetang image is proposed because the character-specific record and exact rendered image URL could not be retrieved during this browser session. The official rights page alone does not identify a candidate asset.

No additional glyph images are proposed: the available externally inspected candidate is sufficient to illustrate the received Shuowen seal form, and other direct historical-form assets were not validated in this pass. Semantic chronology and Tang/Song grammaticalization claims from the dossier were not re-researched in this image-focused pass. The old initial queries cited in the dossier are not counted as this turn's web activity.

items.period: Received Shuowen small-seal tradition; the SVG itself was uploaded in 2017
items.tradition: Small seal script, modern vector redraw
items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 了 in the Shuowen seal-script style. The received Shuowen entry analyzes it as pictographic and says it is formed from 子 without arms; Duan Yucai later explains the graph through crossed legs. The redraw illustrates the received seal form, not an excavated artifact or settled referent.
items.alt: Black seal-style strokes forming the character 了 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: This is a directly identified, reusable character-specific seal-style image. It can anchor the Shuowen form while the caption preserves that the historical interpretation and depicted referent remain disputed.
items.rights: Wikimedia Commons file page states the SVG representation is public domain; attribution appreciated but not required. Modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

limitations.text: The candidate depicts a modern redrawing of a received Shuowen seal-script form; it cannot establish the original referent or date of first use.
The official Xiaoxuetang database offers CC0 reuse for glyph images and attributes obtained through its query interface, but no specific 了 query asset was retrieved in this run, so none is selected.
